title: SQL vs NoSQL
description: Understand when to choose SQL vs NoSQL databases.

options.explanation: Some NoSQL databases support joins (MongoDB $lookup, Couchbase N1QL). The distinction is that NoSQL databases typically don't enforce referential integrity and denormalization is preferred over joins for performance.

options.text: SQL databases are better suited when you need ACID transactions across multiple entities
options.explanation: SQL databases provide native ACID transactions across tables. While some NoSQL databases support transactions (MongoDB multi-document), SQL databases are purpose-built for complex transactional workloads with referential integrity.

options.text: NoSQL databases are always faster than SQL databases
options.explanation: Speed depends on access patterns. SQL with proper indexes can outperform NoSQL for complex queries with joins. NoSQL excels at simple key-value lookups and document retrieval at scale.

options.text: You should always start with NoSQL for new projects
options.explanation: SQL is often the better default — it provides flexibility for evolving schemas, built-in data integrity, and powerful querying. Choose NoSQL when you have specific needs: massive scale, flexible schema, or access patterns that don't fit relational models.
